measurements.name: ab-wildfire-ia-escape
measurements.built_from: the Government of Alberta's pinned Historical wildfire data 2006-2025 CSV (sha256 8b6ed447ab0f958dbe845a53dc15362b8ef5c0810ad9420d2143f9f5ee010a72, 10,400,030 bytes; open.alberta.ca Cloudflare-challenges plain HTTP clients, so the publisher fetch used the supported browser channel and the build asserts the digest)
measurements.grain: one row per assessed wildfire in Alberta's Forest Protection Area, at the publisher's own initial-assessment instant (assessment_datetime, read as America/Edmonton local operational time, confirmed against the official 2016 Horse River review)

population.eligibility: assessment-based, not outcome-conditioned: every discovered wildfire is assessed (100% coverage measured), so all @@TOTAL@@ assessed FPA wildfires 2006-2025 are rows; winter (Nov-Feb) rows kept and counted (@@WINTER@@); 356 winter carryover fires assessed in the year after their record year move with their assessment instant
population.splits_rule: assessment instant's calendar year (America/Edmonton local operational time)

label.definition: escape: final area burned (current_size, the publisher's 'final area burned of the wildfire') at or above 100 ha, on the current compilation's recorded value (>= 100.0, exact on the recorded decimal); threshold-flip exposure from post-hoc area revision is bounded by the measured 89 fires within +-20% of the threshold
label.threshold_note: escape from initial attack read as final area burned >= 100 ha (inside the publisher's size-class D band); 4/40/200 ha variants measured at discovery and recorded in the candidate record; the threshold was fixed before any score and never re-tuned

known_event_fixture.name: 2016 Horse River Fire (MWF009): final area burned 485,123.6 ha in the publisher's record
known_event_fixture.source: asserted in-build against the pinned CSV ((2016, MWF009) current_size 485,123.6 -> escape 1) and corroborated by the Government of Alberta's official review (open.alberta.ca, 'A Review of the 2016 Horse River Wildfire', March 2017, dataset 7cc619bd-56ce-488e-b007-cada28430589), which documents detection at 16:03h MDT on 2016-05-01 - the record's naive local timestamp - under control 2016-07-04 and extinguished 2017-08-02, matching the record's milestone dates; nine further named fires asserted at their publisher-documented final sizes

revision_sensitivity.note: fires within +-20% of the 100 ha threshold bound the post-hoc area-revision label-flip exposure; the publisher documents in-place revision of area burned (spring aerial-photography interpretation)

cross_checks.season_note: current CSV hectares vs the publisher's own season PDFs: <=1.0% for 2020-2024; 2019 differs by -10.4%, consistent with the dictionary's documented spring aerial-photography revision - direct aggregate evidence that the archive is a revised current compilation
cross_checks.timezone_confirmation: official 2016 Horse River review: detected 16:03h MDT 2016-05-01; record REPORTED_DATE 2016-05-01 16:03 naive local

secondary_containment_not_shipped.note: measured diagnostics of the secondary formulation only; the shipped target is escape. The 42.0% already-controlled-at-assessment stratum needs its own design decision and would be a separate task instance

runner_contract_probe.materialize_note: the runner workdir is materialized from the PUBLIC splits only; the private holdout is fetched so --accept can run over the full artifact but is never copied into a workdir

references.measured_on: the identical 5,707 eval rows (2016-2020), post-acceptance, every rate table estimated from train (2006-2015) only; the holdout was never opened
references.protocol: pre-registered: metrics (rank AUC, Brier), references (majority constant, persistence analogue = assessment_hectares, calendar/identity prior from train, full-feature L2 logistic), eval window 2016-2020, day-cluster bootstrap 500 resamples - all fixed before any score was seen; holdout never opened

majority_constant.note: constant score: no ranking information; the AUC is the coin-flip null 0.5 by construction

persistence_assessment_hectares.brier_note: not reported: the persistence analogue is a raw size in hectares, not a probability; Brier is undefined for it

full_minus_persistence.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

full_minus_calendar.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

persistence_minus_calendar.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

references.full_model_note: a simple L2 logistic reference over all shipped features (rare levels pooled at 30 train rows, median imputation with missing indicators, standardized by train statistics), not a tuned model; benchmark agents build their own

ladder: Runner-contract baseline (benchmark train.py + validate.sh, one XGBoost pass)
persistence analogue (assessment_hectares, the observed size at the instant)
calendar/identity prior (train rate per month x forest_area)
construction-time full-feature L2 logistic (simple reference, supplementary)
majority-class accuracy (constant fitted on train, vs eval labels)

construction_full_minus_persistence.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

construction_full_minus_calendar.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

construction_persistence_minus_calendar.note: identical eval rows; an interval containing zero is an inconclusive difference, not parity

supplementary_model_vs_logistic_referenc.note: supplementary only: both are models, so this is not a deciding member; the pre-registered rule compares the model against the baselines above

comparison.verdict_scope: eval split only (assessment years 2016-2020); the sealed holdout (2021-2025) was not evaluated and no holdout figure exists or is implied
comparison.interpretation: Headroom is demonstrated under the pre-registered rule - the runner-contract model beats every triad member with a day-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero in its favour, on eval 2016-2020 only; the holdout (2021-2025) is sealed and has never been scored. The honest reading travels with the number: the persistence analogue (the fire's own observed size at assessment) ranks escape at 0.9096 on its own, and the construction-time simple logistic reference's edge over it is INCONCLUSIVE (+0.0111, CI [-0.0292, 0.0514], interval contains zero). No figure from this dataset may be quoted without the comparison above beside it. No re-tuning of threshold, window, label or features happened after any score.

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one wildfire escape prediction at its own assessment instant; features are the publisher's own assessment record and the runner predicts row-wise from the shipped columns. Labeled eval is development/validation; private holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: the publisher ships a single current compilation (no historical per-fire vintages, no first-publication ledger), so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed - retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

vintage.evidence: the archive is one living compilation (portal updated 2026-02-17, covering through 2025); the dictionary documents in-place revision of area burned (spring aerial-photography interpretation removes waterbodies and unburnt islands), cause (under-investigation -> final) and location (assessment GPS -> confirmed ignition area). Aggregate evidence measured: the 2019 published season total was 883,411 ha while the current archive carries 791,838 ha (-10.4%). Label-flip exposure is bounded: 89 fires lie within +-20% of the 100 ha threshold (measured). Every shipped feature is the current-vintage value of a field documented at/before the assessment instant; no as-of value is claimed

selection.evidence: membership is fixed at the assessment instant: a row exists because the wildfire was discovered and assessed, never because of an outcome; no completeness or volume gate is applied (unlike panel releases), there is no censoring rule (every row carries a terminal status), and both label values are retained in every window. The population definition (all FPA wildfires) is stable; the detection channel mix drifts (lookouts 34% of 2006 -> 21% of 2025; unplanned 42% -> 59%) and ships as the detection_agent_type feature

measurements.prevalence_shift: positive rate rises into the holdout (1.87% train 2006-2015 -> 1.82% eval 2016-2020 -> 4.11% holdout 2021-2025, which contains the 2023 record season): documented non-stationarity, recorded as a property of the data, not repaired
measurements.clustering: positives arrive on the same extreme fire-weather day, so distinct positive assessment dates are the conservative independent-observation count (156/79/128) and every interval in the comparison is day-clustered (cluster = assessment_date)

data_compilation.scope: Our contribution - the all-cause assessment-instant population frame (every assessed Forest Protection Area wildfire 2006-2025, winter rows kept and counted, eligibility assessment-based with no outcome-conditioned rule), the derived binary escape label (final area burned >= 100 ha on the current compilation's recorded value), the at-instant feature derivations (elapsed hours from reported/discovered/estimated-start to the assessment instant, calendar and cyclical day-of-year fields, forest-area prefix, coordinate passthrough), the column policy that excludes every post-instant and label-source family, the winter-carryover split rule (assessment instant's calendar year, America/Edmonton local operational time) and the temporal partition (train 2006-2015 / eval 2016-2020 / holdout 2021-2025) - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the Government of Alberta's wildfire records keep their own designation and remain subject to the Open Government Licence - Alberta v2.2, whose attribution requirement carries through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source_data.status: One preserved upstream instrument, not relicensed. The Government of Alberta's Historical wildfire data 2006-2025 (per-fire incident records, Forest Protection Area) is licensed under the Open Government Licence - Alberta v2.2, with its attribution requirement, non-endorsement clause, no-warranty terms and (where applicable) personal-information exemption. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own assessment-instant record (assessment size, rate of spread, fire behaviour type, position on slope, in-situ weather over the fire, FBP fuel type, detection channel), pre-instant timing fields and location, plus our derived label, elapsed-time features and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is neither the Government of Alberta's official product nor endorsed by it.

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.
